land.text: Syphax's Masaesyli kingdom in the west (capital Siga), given to Masinissa after Zama in 202 BC; the Massylii kingdom at Cirta was Masinissa's own

predecessors.note: No Cliopatria row for the Masaesyli (about 213-202 BC); a dossier for them is needed (counterparts_needing_dossiers).

land.text: eastern Numidia, annexed in 46 BC as the Roman province Africa Nova

successors.note: Western Numidia stayed under Bocchus I's Mauretania from 105 BC (Jugurtha-war page); the Numidia page also has a rump western Numidia annexed into Africa Nova after Arabio died in 40 BC, which no Cliopatria row covers.

capitals.name: Cirta (Constantine)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Cirta (today Constantine, Algeria)'; the Massylii capital, 'later the capital of Masinissa's united Numidia'. Siga was the Masaesyli capital under Syphax.

correction.text: the Massylii kingdom at Cirta united with Syphax's Masaesyli kingdom after Zama (202 BC), 'the Moulouya River to the west, the Mediterranean to the north, and Saharan regions to the south'; Tripolitania not yet Numidian (taken 'by 158 BC')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the kingdom in -197 but the page's infobox gives 'Established: 202 BC', and the Tripolitanian coast (Lepcis Magna) is said to be conquered only 'by 158 BC'. The infobox gives no area. The shape is the -197 shape without Tripolitania; the extent in the Sahara is unverified.

correction.text: unchanged shape, but valid only from 158 BC to 145 BC, when it includes 'Lepcis Magna and the Tripolitanian coast'; before that the new -202 keyframe applies; the 152 BC seizure of Carthaginian territory is within it

keyframe_review.note: 306,737 km2; the page has no area figure to compare. Years change, not outline: Cliopatria draws Tripolitania from -197, the page has it conquered 'by 158 BC'. The -152 border move against Carthage is in the ledger; the page names no towns, so the shape is kept.

306,762 km2, the same outline after Carthage's fall in 146. The page does not describe Numidian gains after the Third Punic War, and the border with Roman Africa is not drawn on any page opened (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid only to 106 BC; from 105 BC the shape without western Numidia (new -105 keyframe) applies

keyframe_review.note: 307,188 km2. The Jugurthine War page says Bocchus 'annexed the western part of Jugurtha's kingdom' in 105 BC (infobox), but Cliopatria keeps the whole kingdom until -92 and cuts it only in -91. The division of 116 BC between Jugurtha (west) and Adherbal (east) is inside this one shape (Jugurtha retook Cirta in 112 per the Jugurtha page).

correction.text: the kingdom without 'the western part of Jugurtha's kingdom' annexed by Bocchus I in 105 BC

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the -91 shape applied 14 years earlier. The page gives no boundary for western Numidia; the Jugurtha page says Bocchus got western Numidia 'extending to the Mulucha River', while the Numidia page says Gauda was 'granted central Numidia' and Hiempsal II and Hiarbas later divided the kingdom. Cliopatria's cut at 5.3 E is therefore its own line.

125,973 km2: eastern and central Numidia, the shape still reaching into Libya (to 18.7 E). The page gives no area; 81 BC: 'Hiempsal II regained his kingdom and was granted Hiarbas's former territory', an inner change that does not alter the outline. Boundary with Bocchus' Mauretania unverified (no page names it).
One year, the same outline as the -91 shape; the Juba I page has Curio sent by Caesar in August 49 BC to take Africa, defeated and killed, with no change of border.

correction.text: unchanged shape, extended one year to 46 BC

keyframe_review.note: Years change only: Cliopatria ends the kingdom in -47; the page has Eastern Numidia 'annexed in 46 BC to create a new Roman province, Africa Nova', and the Juba I page has Juba's death in 46.

region.text: the Massylii kingdom in the east with its capital at Cirta

ledger.note: 202 BC: Masinissa becomes first king of a united Numidia. Infobox 'Established: 202 BC'; 'Scipio proclaimed Masinissa king of all Numidia' at Cirta in 203, after the capture of Syphax; the Massylii 'held the eastern kingdom, with its capital at Cirta'.

region.text: the Masaesyli kingdom of Syphax in the west (capital Siga), up to the Moulouya

ledger.note: 202 BC: Masinissa receives Syphax's kingdom after Zama. 'for his services Masinissa received the Kingdom of Syphax'; he 'then ruled both the Massylii and the Masaesyli' (Masinissa page). The Numidia page says he 'took control of much of Syphax's territory' and made the Masaesyli king a vassal. The page does not draw the Masaesyli boundary.

region.text: Bokkar's kingdom, 'what is now Morocco' with its capital at Tingis

ledger.note: 202 BC: Mauretania becomes Masinissa's vassal. 'Following the capture of Syphax, the King Bokkar, ruler of what is now Morocco with his capital based in Tingis, had become a vassal of Masinissa.' The sentence has no date; a French reference note on the page dates it: 'En 202 avant Jesus-Christ, apres la capture de Syphax, il devint le vassal de Massinissa'. The vassal keeps its own land, drawn in the lighter tint inside the Numidian sphere (the vassal events belong to the suzerain's ledger, so the mauretania dossier has none). fx-54 (3 Nov 2026), from the fx-50 handoff.

region.text: Lepcis Magna and the Tripolitanian coast

ledger.note: By 158 BC: Masinissa holds the Tripolitanian coast. The page says he 'had, by 158 BC, conquered Lepcis Magna and the Tripolitanian coast'; the year is a latest date, so the conquest may be earlier. Cliopatria draws it from -197.

region.text: 'more Carthaginian territory' along the Numidian border; the page names no towns (earlier it notes Masinissa 'hadn't laid his hands yet on the fertile lands of the Emporia')

ledger.note: 152: Masinissa seizes more Carthaginian land. 'When Masinissa seized more Carthaginian territory in 152 BC, political tensions within the city intensified.' The land is a band along the frontier by my reading; Carthage's loss event belongs to its own dossier.

region.text: Carthaginian lands invaded by Masinissa, with the siege of Oroscopa

ledger.note: 151: the Numidian-Carthaginian fighting at Oroscopa. Masinissa 'invaded Carthaginian lands in 151 BC with an army of 52,000 men, besieging a town called' Oroscopa; the Masinissa page has him defeat the Carthaginians there. The page does not place Oroscopa, so the zone is the frontier band.

148 BC: the tie is closed at Masinissa's death, a bridge. 'he died early in 148 BC without a breach in the alliance.' The page says nothing about Bokkar or his kingdom after the capture of Syphax, so no page dates the end of the vassalage; Mauretania next appears as Bocchus I's kingdom taking western Numidia in 105 BC (ledger -105 loss to mauretania). Confidence 1 for the end date.

region.text: the Numidian-Carthaginian frontier, which disappears with Carthage

ledger.note: 146: Carthage is destroyed and the border war ends with it. The Masinissa page has the Third Punic War 149-146 start 'after Numidian raids on about seventy Carthaginian towns' (Livy); Masinissa died early in 148, 'without a breach in the alliance' with Rome. Cliopatria keeps a Carthage shape to -145.

region.text: the eastern half of Numidia with Cirta, Adherbal's capital: Jugurtha received 'the better, more fertile and populous western half of Numidia' and Adherbal the east (Jugurthine War page)

ledger.note: 116: Rome partitions Numidia between Jugurtha and Adherbal. 'A Senate commission, led by former consul Lucius Opimius, began dividing Numidia in 116 BC. Jugurtha received the better, more fertile and populous western half'; the Numidia page gives 114 BC, the Jugurtha page 'probably in 116'. Both halves are one Cliopatria shape; keep one colour.

region.text: Cirta, Adherbal's capital, and the eastern half

ledger.note: 112: Jugurtha takes Cirta and reunites the kingdom. 'By 112 BC, Jugurtha resumed the war and trapped Adherbal in Cirta'; he 'captured Cirta' and Adherbal was killed. The Jugurthine War page puts Adherbal's retreat into Cirta in 113 and does not date the fall.

region.text: western Numidia: the part of the -110 shape that the -91 shape no longer holds (the page names 'the western part of Jugurtha's kingdom', not a boundary)

ledger.note: 105: Bocchus I gets western Numidia for betraying Jugurtha. Bocchus handed Jugurtha to Sulla and 'annexed the western part of Jugurtha's kingdom' (infobox 105 BC); the Jugurtha page has the land 'extending to the Mulucha River'; the Numidia page words it: 'western Numidia, which was now called Mauretania, was added to the lands of Bocchus I'. Cliopatria cuts the shape in -91.
46: Caesar annexes Numidia as Africa Nova after Juba I's defeat and death. 'Eastern Numidia was annexed in 46 BC to create a new Roman province, Africa Nova.'

region.text: the kingdom's last territory, eastern Numidia

ledger.note: 46: the kingdom ends with Juba I, who 'reigned from 60 to 46 BC' and died in 46 after the African campaign (he fled the field at Thapsus, then took his own life in a suicide pact with Petreius).

wars.name: Numidian-Carthaginian border war

zones.text: Carthaginian lands along the Numidian frontier, Oroscopa

wars.outcome: Masinissa seizes Carthaginian territory in 152, invades in 151 (Oroscopa) and defeats the Carthaginians; Carthage's war on Numidia breaches its treaty with Rome and leads to the Third Punic War.
wars.note: The Masinissa page: 151 BC defeat at Oroscopa; 'Carthage's war against Numidia breached its treaty with Rome'; Third Punic War 149-146, Numidia on Rome's side.

wars.name: Jugurthine War

zones.text: western Numidia: the part of the -110 shape that the -91 shape no longer holds (the page names 'the western part of Jugurtha's kingdom', not a boundary)

wars.outcome: Rome fights Jugurtha 112-105 (Bestia's peace, Albinus' surrender in 110, Metellus 109, Marius from 107); Bocchus I of Mauretania hands Jugurtha to Sulla in 105 and annexes the western part of the kingdom.
wars.note: No page opened says Rome held Numidian ground during the war, so no contest event is recorded; the territorial result is the 105 loss. Reviewer (af-02-b, 2026-10-19): start set to 111 BC, the page's infobox 'Date: 111-105 BC' (the Senate 'declared war on Jugurtha in 111 BC').

wars.name: Caesar's Civil War in Africa
wars.outcome: Juba I defeats Curio (August 49), joins Scipio, flees from Thapsus and dies in 46; Bocchus II and Publius Sittius invade Numidia from the west; Numidia becomes Africa Nova.
wars.note: The Juba I page does not date Thapsus, Bocchus II's invasion or the annexation; the 46 BC annexation is from the Numidia page.

certainty.note: All Numidian frontiers are approximate: the Moulouya to the west, the Saharan fringe to the south, and the Carthaginian/Roman African frontier are named on the pages but never drawn; the Roman province border after 146 is the only quasi-fixed line.

sources.title: Numidia
sources.note: Identity, founding 202 BC, capital Cirta, Tripolitania by 158, 152/151 Carthage, 114 division, Bocchus, Gauda, 46 BC Africa Nova. No infobox area.

sources.title: Jugurtha
sources.note: 116 division, 112 Cirta, 105 Bocchus and the Mulucha.

sources.title: Masinissa
sources.note: 206-202 reign, Kingdom of Syphax 202, 201 treaty, Oroscopa 151, Third Punic War.

sources.title: Jugurthine War
sources.note: 116 division, 113 retreat to Cirta, 105 settlement with Bocchus, Roman province 46.

notes: Cliopatria's start (-197) is five years after the page's 202 BC; its Libya outline is drawn from -197 though Tripolitania is only 'by 158 BC'; its 105 BC loss to Bocchus comes in -91 and its end (-47) a year early. Disagreement: the Numidia page puts the Senate's division in 114 BC, the Jugurtha page 'probably 116', the Jugurthine War page 116. The Masinissa page gives 206 for the start of his reign over the Massylii. Masinissa 'Bokkar of present-day Morocco also became his vassal' (Masinissa page, undated): not recorded as a vassal event because the page gives no year. Neither the Masaesyli (Syphax) nor Adherbal's eastern Numidia have a dossier; Masaesyli needs one. The Numidia page's rump 'western Numidia' under Arabio to 40 BC and the kingdom of Cirta under Sittius are not Cliopatria rows. Ruler strip left out: only Masinissa (202-148), Jugurtha (118-105) and Juba I (60-46) are on pages opened, with Micipsa, Gauda and Hiempsal II undated there. Gazetteer note: 'Numidia', 'Constantinois', 'Tripolitania' resolve; no other name used. Pages did not give the area of Numidia in km2, so the area check against Cliopatria (307k then 126k km2) was not possible. Page budget (5) fully used; the Roman Africa border after 146 and Cirta's kingdom under Sittius unexplored.
